findings.summary: CP-HI-03 can be bypassed with caller-supplied run metadata
findings.detail: activateManifest authorizes replacement solely from via.runKind strings. Sequence: store H2, then call activateManifest(project,H2,{runKind:'CONTRACT_CHANGE',runId:null}); the active manifest changes without proving that a matching project run exists, reached COMPLETED, or passed gates for H2. This contradicts Integration §10.4.
findings.suggestedFix: Require a non-null runId and transactionally verify the run belongs to the project, has the required kind and completed exact-candidate gate evidence containing the new manifest digest.

findings.summary: The supposedly pinned manifest can be overwritten at any time
findings.detail: pinManifest performs an unconditional update with no run-state, authorization, expected-old-value, or run-kind check. Sequence: dispatch under H1, store H2, call pinManifest(runId,H2); the authoritative pin now reports H2 despite no CONTRACT_CHANGE completion. This defeats CP-HI-03's immutable dispatch-time contract pin.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove this unrestricted mutator or make pinning a dispatch-only compare-and-set operation. Contract changes must create a new gated run and affect only later runs.

findings.summary: A fabricated CEO session can complete a run
findings.detail: submitCeoDecision only checks that the supplied ceoSessionId is not recorded as the run's CTO/reviewer. It never requires that the ID is an existing, current CEO binding. Passing an arbitrary unknown ID therefore satisfies independence and can transition READY_FOR_CEO_REVIEW to COMPLETED. resolveEscalation has the same caller-supplied-ID defect.
findings.suggestedFix: Authenticate the caller and require its session ID, incarnation, role key, and binding generation to match the current active CEO binding before accepting either decision.

findings.summary: CP-HI-07 owner authority is replaced by an unauthenticated method call
findings.detail: recordOwnerDecision accepts no owner identity or authorization proof and unconditionally writes actor:'owner'. Sequence: any caller invokes it with approved:true for each gate item; humanGateStatus then treats the owner-only gate as satisfied. CtoLifecycle.suspendProject similarly trusts a bare ownerApproved boolean.
findings.suggestedFix: Accept owner decisions only from an authenticated owner ingress, bind proof to the exact decision/run, and persist the verified principal or authorization receipt. Never infer owner authority from a boolean.

findings.summary: Task execution authority is not bound to the task's run
findings.detail: startExecution never compares input.runId with task.runId, and the schema independently references both IDs. An owner of run A can submit taskId from run B, producing an execution attributed to A while marking B's task RUNNING. finishExecution likewise accepts only an execution ID, enabling cross-run completion through an otherwise authorized run-A request.
findings.suggestedFix: Require task.runId === input.runId, validate the current pinned run owner inside the transaction, and require authenticated run/session/generation context for activity and finish operations.

findings.summary: A successful task without the mandatory result receipt passes completeness
findings.detail: finishExecution permits status SUCCEEDED with resultDigest null. completeness only rejects unfinished tasks and RUNNING executions, so that task counts as complete and ProductionGate.buildPacket proceeds. This directly violates the §25.2 finished-receipt contract and CP-HI-08.
findings.suggestedFix: Reject SUCCEEDED without a non-empty resultDigest and have completeness verify a valid finished receipt for every expected task/latest attempt.

findings.summary: The graph can change after the production-ready packet is frozen
findings.detail: submit has no run-state or candidate-freeze restriction. Sequence: finish all tasks, build the packet, let the run enter READY_FOR_CEO_REVIEW, then submit a new pending task; submitCeoDecision does not recompute completeness and can complete the run with unfinished work. This bypasses §34.3 and CP-HI-08.
findings.suggestedFix: Permit graph mutation only in an authorized ACTIVE planning phase. Any later mutation must supersede the candidate and packet and return the run to ACTIVE; CEO confirmation should revalidate completeness atomically.

findings.summary: A checkout can be registered under another repository's identity
findings.detail: When input.identity is supplied it overrides the normalized observed remote without comparison. A bootstrap can bind checkout A using repository B's manifest identity; snapshots and verification then report B while reading and testing A. That invalidates exact repository evidence under CP-HI-06 and CP-HI-08.
findings.suggestedFix: When a remote exists, require the supplied normalized identity to equal the normalized observed remote. Treat remote-less local bindings as a separate explicitly authorized case.

findings.summary: Normal switchover can revoke a CTO that acquired a new active run
findings.detail: prepareSwitchover neither requires the outgoing session to be DRAINING nor establishes a durable dispatch barrier; it checks active runs only once. Sequence: prepare at zero runs, dispatch a new run to the still-READY old CTO, then acknowledge the handoff. acknowledgeHandoff does not recheck zero active runs or compare the current binding with from_generation, so it switches and stops the old session, leaving the run pinned to a revoked owner.
findings.suggestedFix: Require and persist DRAINING before preparation, keep dispatch blocked, and in the ACK transaction compare-and-set the expected outgoing generation and recheck that it owns zero active runs.

findings.summary: Old execution receipts can overwrite newer attempts
findings.detail: finishExecution does not require the execution to be RUNNING or the latest task attempt. Sequence: attempt 1 fails, attempt 2 fails or runs, then attempt 1 is replayed as SUCCEEDED; the task is changed to SUCCEEDED and dependents become READY despite the newer attempt. A completed execution is therefore mutable rather than audit-only.
findings.suggestedFix: Condition the update on status='RUNNING' and task.attempt_count matching the execution attempt. Reject or audit-only all duplicate and superseded receipts.

findings.summary: Production gate publication and CEO notification are not atomic
findings.detail: The approval, immutable production packet, run transition, and notification enqueue are separate writes. An illegal transition or crash can leave an authoritative packet without the state change, or READY_FOR_CEO_REVIEW without its notification. notify also silently returns when no CEO binding exists while recording a CEO_NOTIFICATION audit event. This violates §30.3 and masks delivery loss.
findings.suggestedFix: Validate first, then transactionally write the approval/packet, transition state, and enqueue a durable notification intent. Missing CEO authority must produce an explicit blocked/critical state, not success.

findings.summary: OWNER_DECISION_REQUIRED has no path back to active execution
findings.detail: submitCeoDecision moves the run to AWAITING_HUMAN, but recordOwnerDecision only stores an artifact and returns. It neither transitions AWAITING_HUMAN to ACTIVE nor enqueues a reply to the CTO, and RunEngine.dispatch does not admit AWAITING_HUMAN. The CP-S55 resume flow therefore stalls indefinitely.
findings.suggestedFix: After an authenticated owner decision satisfies the required items, transactionally transition AWAITING_HUMAN to ACTIVE and enqueue the fenced continuation message, or provide an equivalent explicit resume operation.

findings.summary: Projectless runs become ACTIVE without an owner
findings.detail: dispatch provisions and pins a binding only when projectId is present, yet create explicitly permits projectless and bootstrap runs. Such a run transitions to ACTIVE with all owner fields null and no dispatch message; subsequent authority checks reject every CTO operation. This violates §11.1 owner pinning and makes the required unregistered/bootstrap flows unusable.
findings.suggestedFix: Resolve and require the appropriate run-scoped/bootstrap CTO binding for projectless runs. Refuse ACTIVE transition unless owner session, generation, incarnation, and role key are all pinned.

findings.summary: Capacity suspend abandons active runs and suppresses cleanup failures
findings.detail: suspendProject sets the project suspended, revokes the CTO binding, and stops the logical session without enumerating, checkpointing, canceling, or changing its active runs. Those runs remain ACTIVE under a revoked owner. Provider stop failures are swallowed with catch(() => undefined), yet the method records success, contradicting §10.4 and CP-HI-08.
findings.suggestedFix: Create durable checkpoints and explicitly transition or queue every active run before revoking the binding. Record cleanup receipts and return an error or critical-system finding when runtime cleanup fails.

findings.summary: Repository drift clears itself after a second observation
findings.detail: observe writes the newly observed head into last_observed_head even when it marks the checkout DRIFTED. A second observation of the unchanged, clean out-of-band head then compares equal and changes the state to IN_SYNC without acknowledgeHead. Unexpected writes are therefore silently accepted as the baseline.
findings.suggestedFix: Keep the trusted baseline head separate from the latest observation. Do not advance the baseline while drifted; only acknowledgeHead after an authorized managed change.

findings.summary: Temporary repository bindings are reused across runs
findings.detail: registerTemporary returns any existing identity without checking registration or temporaryForRun. If run A created the temporary record, run B receives the same record still scoped to A and can attach it because no downstream scope check exists. This contradicts §16.3's run-only temporary binding.
findings.suggestedFix: Return a registered global binding normally, but deny or create a separate run-binding relation when an existing TEMPORARY record belongs to another run.

findings.summary: Lexically identical write paths bypass the exact-path hard reject
findings.detail: normalizePath only strips leading './' and '/'. Two runs can claim src/../README.md and README.md, or a/./b and a/b, and both rows are accepted although they name the same repository file. This defeats the §23.2 exact declared-path collision guarantee.
findings.suggestedFix: Canonicalize with repository-relative POSIX semantics, reject absolute/empty/escaping paths and platform aliases, and store only the canonical representation used by the write guard.

findings.summary: Any claim ID can be released without holder authorization or a transaction
findings.detail: release accepts only claimId and never compares the caller's run, session, or binding generation with the stored holder. Thus an owner of run A can release run B's claim and then acquire its resource. The select/update/audit sequence is also outside db.tx, despite §30.3 requiring claim release atomicity.
findings.suggestedFix: Require expected run/session/generation, validate them against the current binding, and perform a conditional HELD-to-RELEASED update plus audit in one immediate transaction.

findings.summary: The gate silently tolerates a missing candidate snapshot artifact
findings.detail: buildPacket treats candidate-snapshot lookup as optional and substitutes an empty changedRepositories list. Verification/review artifacts can therefore produce a production-ready packet without the authoritative snapshot artifact the packet claims to summarize. CP-HI-08 requires this evidence absence to fail closed.
findings.suggestedFix: Require the exact CANDIDATE_SNAPSHOT artifact, validate its digest/run/repository coverage, and deny packet creation when it is absent or inconsistent.
